t: Of the funds available under this heading in Public Law 103–332 and any unobligated balances from funds appropriated under this heading in prior years, $9,571,000 are rescinded.

fable.w: This section only rescinds previously appropriated funds. It involves no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government takes part in any decision. There is no real tempting reading here; the reference to Public Law 103-332 just identifies the source of the funds.

opus.w: This section only rescinds $9,571,000 in appropriated and unobligated funds. It does not involve any party outside the federal government in a federal decision. There is no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking authority or right to sue, so nothing in it fits the definition of participation.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a simple rescission of appropriated funds. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, the public, or private entities). The action is taken by Congress (inside the government) and affects federal budget allocations without requiring input from outsiders.
qwen_chat.s: Of the funds available under this heading in Public Law 103–332 and any unobligated balances from funds appropriated under this heading in prior years, $9,571,000 are rescinded.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that rescinding funds is a "decision" that affects the public, but the text itself contains no mechanism for public input, consultation, or participation in that decision. It is a unilateral legislative action regarding budget execution.
